quote: A random variable Z is said to be greater than Y in the: (a) Stochastic order (Y <=st Z) if G_Z(z) <= G_Y(z) for all z; (b) Hazard rate order (Y <=hr Z) if h_Z(z) <= h_Y(z) for all z; (c) Mean residual order (Y <=mlr Z) if m_Z(z) <= m_Y(z) for all z; (d) Likelihood ratio order (Y <=lr Z) if g_Z(z)/g_Y(z) is an increasing function of z. The following results (Shaked and Shanthikumar 1994) are well known: Z <=lr Y => Z <=hr Y => Z <=mrl Y => Z <=st Y.
family: Exponentiated Inverse Power Lindley distribution EIPLD(alpha, beta, theta)

quote: Theorem 4: Let Y ~ EIPLD(alpha1, beta1, theta1) and Z ~ EIPLD(alpha2, beta2, theta2). If beta1 = beta2 and theta2 >= theta1 (or if beta2 >= beta1 and theta1 = theta2) then (Y <=lr Z) for all z. Setting alpha1 = alpha2: Case 1: for beta1 = beta2 and theta2 >= theta1 we obtained d/dz [g_Z(z)/g_Y(z)] as an increasing function of z. Case 2: beta2 >= beta1 and theta1 = theta2 we obtained d/dz [g_Z(z)/g_Y(z)] as an increasing function of z. This implies that Y <=lr Z for all z. Hence Y <=hr Z, Y <=mrl Z and Y <=st Z.
compared: two EIPLD variables with common alpha, differing in beta or theta

hypotheses.text: alpha1 = alpha2 (imposed in proof) and either (beta1 = beta2, theta2 >= theta1) or (beta2 >= beta1, theta1 = theta2)

conclusion.direction: Y <=_lr Z; hence Y <=_hr Z, Y <=_mrl Z and Y <=_st Z

ambiguity: Theorem statement omits alpha1 = alpha2 but the proof explicitly sets alpha1 = alpha2 before considering the two cases; recorded as a hypothesis.
